assumptions: Rule matching is on the path relative to incoming/ (study folder included), with literal, case-sensitive substring tests; only the 'ar' folder name is case-insensitive.
Data format precedence for anonymised folders follows the same order as for normal folders: adam, then sdtm, then raw/restricted_raw.
If several folders are named 'ar', the first one is used for the CDAR reporting level.
For ANON the 'ia' last part is converted like CDAP: ia500 becomes ia_500.
'/med', '/cdap', '/idap', '/anon' are plain substring tests, so e.g. /medical also counts as /med.
Files directly in a study folder (e.g. incoming/S1/a.pdf) are not skipped; they fall under DEFAULT and keep their path.
A file whose only '.' is a leading dot (e.g. .hidden) counts as having an extension.
No minimum file age is applied; files still being uploaded may be picked up. The 45-minute cron fires at minutes 00 and 45 of each hour, so run gaps are uneven (45 and 15 minutes).
Files in error/ and files that already exist at the target are overwritten when the same key is produced again.
S3 tag values over 256 characters cannot be set; that counts as a tagging failure (warning only).
